I became a member of our church in 1978, when it was known as St. Thomas Church. Having been born and raised in the Orthodox faith, I have always cherished my connection to the Church. Over the years, I have witnessed our parish's journey from 38th and Chestnut Streets to Torresdale Avenue and finally to our beautiful church in Bensalem. Among my treasured memories are the blessings of H.G. Barnabas Thirumeni and H.G. Makarios Thirumeni, especially the blessing given to my son and other children to serve in the sanctuary. As we celebrate our Golden Jubilee, my greatest hope is that future generations will remain steadfast in the Orthodox faith, actively participate in MGOCSM, and continue to strengthen and grow our beloved parish.

blocks.text:
Our journey with this church began in 2007 when we first walked through the doors as college students. Back then, it was just a place to worship, but it quickly became the foundation for our entire future. This is where we grew, dreamed, and eventually decided to build a life and family together.

Over the last nearly two decades, the people here have truly become our family. The friends we made in those early years have grown into a lifelong, supportive community.

Our family has since been blessed with two wonderful children. Sharing our faith with them has been the greatest joy of our journey. Both of our kids were baptized by Shibu Achen in this sanctuary, surrounded by the love of this congregation. Today, they look forward to attending Sunday school each week, learning the same values that have anchored us for so long. We are profoundly grateful for this church home, which has shaped our past, blesses our present, and continues to guide our future.
blocks.sign: The Milton Family (Marcus, Meryl, Nithya and Basil)

blocks.title: A journey that began with a baptism and grew into a beautiful sense of faith, friendship, and belonging
blocks.text:
When we moved to New Jersey in 2020, the world looked very different. The pandemic had brought life to a standstill, and being new to the area, we were searching not only for a church but also for a community where our family could feel at home.

During that time, a priest from the West Coast told us about St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church, Bensalem. Since we were also thinking about having our little one baptized, he encouraged us to reach out to the church. That recommendation turned out to be the beginning of a beautiful journey for our family.

When we first approached our Parish Vicar, Rev. Fr. Shibu Venad Mathai (Shibu Achen), he welcomed us with incredible warmth and kindness. When he learned that we had moved from Mumbai, he immediately began introducing us to other Hindi-speaking families in the parish. It was a simple gesture, but for a family that was new to the area, it meant so much. The Managing Committee and the entire church community welcomed us so wholeheartedly that, from the very beginning, we felt that we belonged.

In October 2020, during a time when gatherings were still very limited, we had the blessing of baptizing our little one at St. Gregorios. With only a small number of parish members and a few of our extended family present, the baptism was held under the guidance of Rev. Fr. Shibu Venad Mathai and Very Rev. K. Mathai Cor Episcopos. Though it was a small gathering, it remains one of the most meaningful memories of our family's journey with the church.

From that day forward, St. Gregorios has become much more than the church we attend on Sundays—it has become our extended family. Our children were welcomed into Sunday School, and we were given opportunities to become involved in different ministries, cultural programs, and church activities. Through these experiences, we have met so many wonderful people, built beautiful friendships, and created memories that we will always cherish.

Over the years, going to church on Sunday has naturally become an important part of our family's life. Our children look forward to Sunday School every week and, most importantly, have formed friendships that we hope will last a lifetime. As parents, it brings us great joy to see them growing up surrounded by faith, friendship, tradition, and a community that cares for them.

Looking back at how our journey began in the uncertain days of 2020, we are deeply grateful that God led us to St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church, Bensalem. The warmth with which we were welcomed continues to be something we treasure. Our parish has played a vital role in shaping our family's life, strengthening our faith, and giving us a true sense of belonging.

What began as a search for a church became the blessing of finding a church family and a home away from home.

members.name: James Varughese
members.title: James Varughese & Family

blocks.text:
As our parish celebrates its Golden Jubilee under the leadership of Rev. Fr. Shibu Venad Mathai, our family—James (Jimmy), Caroline, Andrew, and Timothy (Timmy) Varughese, together with our father, Gheevarughese Mathai (Babu)—reflects with profound gratitude on the journey that has bound us to this holy sanctuary. A pinnacle moment of this Golden Jubilee celebration was the laying on of hands of Andrew by the supreme head of the Church, H.H. Moran Mar Baselios Marthoma Mathews III, to enter the holy altar. Though our sister Jenny, her husband Sandeep, and their children Amelia and Luke relocated to Tennessee in March of this year, our spiritual roots in this parish community remain unshakeable.

Over the years, God has granted our family the privilege of serving Him at the parish, regional, and diocesan levels. From serving as OVBS Coordinator, Diocese OVBS Committee Member, Sunday School Teacher and Registrar, Youth League Treasurer, MGOCSM Council Member, Parish Committee member, and member of both the Board of Directors and Mission Board, to contributing to St. Joseph's Forum, MMVS, STG, Christmas Carol, and Gregorian Harmony, as well as serving as Acolytes at the altar, each ministry has anchored our lives more deeply in the Church.

With loving hearts, we treasure the sacred memory of our dear mother and a founding member of the parish, Annamma Gheevarughese (Kunjumol), and hold fond memories of our founding vicar, V. Rev. Fr. K. Mathai Cor-Episcopos. We also honor the revered Hierarchs who guided our path: L.L. H.G. Thomas Mar Makarios, who laid hands on Jimmy to enter the altar; L.L. H.G. Mathews Mar Barnabas, who tenderly shepherded the American Diocese during the early growth of the MGOCSM; and L.L. H.G. Zachariah Mar Theophilus, who blessed and solemnized our Holy Matrimony. May their memory be eternal.

In the midst of life's present struggles and uncertainties, holding fast to our Orthodox faith and the Holy Sacraments is not merely our tradition—it is our hope and strength. May the Almighty continue to shower His divine grace upon our parish for generations to come.

blocks.text:
When many of us came to the United States of America from Kerala, we brought with us more than dreams and hopes for a better future. We also brought our culture, traditions, memories, and most importantly, the Orthodox faith that was passed down to us by our parents and grandparents. It is the faith we grew up with, the faith that has guided us through different stages of our lives, and the faith we now hope to pass on to our children.

Starting a life in a new country came with many changes and challenges. Through it all, we are grateful that we have been able to continue living and growing in our Malankara Orthodox faith. Through SGMOC, we found more than a church. We found a spiritual home and a community where we could pray together, celebrate together, and support one another. Over the years, this parish has become an important part of our life and our journey here in America.

One of the greatest blessings for us as parents is seeing our children grow up in this same faith. It brings us joy to see them attend Sunday School, participate in Holy Qurbana and church celebrations, and spend time with their church friends. Through these experiences, they are learning about God, our faith, and the traditions that have been part of our families for generations. At the same time, they are building friendships and creating memories that we hope they will carry with them throughout their lives.

As SGMOC celebrates 50 years, we are especially grateful for those who came before us. Their faith, hard work, and sacrifices gave families like ours a place to call our spiritual home. They passed this faith on to us, and now it is our turn to pass it on to our children. Our hope and prayer is that they will carry it with them wherever life takes them and, one day, pass it on to the generations that follow.

blocks.title: Golden Jubilee Notes
blocks.text:
It is with immense gratitude that we, Shobha and I, thank God for providing us the opportunity to be part of this Malankara Orthodox Church from its inception as the first parish in Philadelphia in 1976. We thank our parents for nurturing us with the zeal and love for the Orthodox Churches we were members of, from our childhood. When we immigrated to this nation of opportunities in the early 70's, we started attending the Ecumenical congregation in Philadelphia, established during the latter part of the 1960s by a good number of Malayalee Christians belonging to different denominations living in the Philadelphia metropolitan region.

1976 was a historical year for the Orthodox Church with the arrival of Rev. Fr. K. Mathai to the US and later to Philadelphia with Mariamma Kochamma and their twin girls. With his initiative, and in response to the demand from most of our Orthodox members, the first Orthodox parish with the name St. Thomas Orthodox Church of India, Philadelphia (STOCI) was established in the city of Philadelphia on the 10th of October 1976. We worshipped in the chapel of the Philadelphia Episcopal Church on 38th and Chestnut Streets. I was one of the members of the first Board of Trustees of the parish. We were also blessed with the birth of our daughter Namita in September 1976.

1984 was another important and memorable year for us. We welcomed the arrival of our twin boys Matthew and Michael. It was also the year that St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church (SGMOC) was formed after the dissolution of STOCI by His Grace Dr. Thomas Mar Makarios, Metropolitan of the American diocese. The majority of the members of the dissolved STOCI parish joined and formed the new SGMOC parish with Mathai Achen as its vicar. The parish bought a small church building on Torresdale Avenue in Philadelphia in 1995.

During the next ten years, the parish membership increased in number, and grew in prominence as one of the most vibrant parishes of the American Diocese. The need for a larger place of worship and space for other spiritual activities and amenities resulted in finding the property on Hulmeville Road in Bensalem, just outside of Philadelphia in 2005. The new SGMOC building was consecrated in May 2009. After Mathai Achen's retirement, Rev. Fr. Shibu Mathai was appointed as the vicar of SGMOC in 2011. The parish has witnessed tremendous growth in membership and spirituality under his leadership.

On a personal note, I was blessed to have had the opportunity to serve the parish as an acolyte as well as a Sunday School teacher, and also as a member in the parish administration for several years.

Our children, Seryna and Mathew, were baptized here. They have been attending SGMOC since they were born. Mathew was an active student at the SGMOC's Sunday school, till he graduated. He, along with his team, won Bible competitions in a row for three times at the Diocesan level. He is now serving as an altar boy. We are thankful for the help and services this church provides to morally educate our children.

Through changing seasons, new buildings, joyful celebrations, and tear-stained prayers, we have walked together, grown together, and carried one another. We are grateful for the generations of love, culture, and community that shaped us — for the friendships that became family, for the memories created in every building, hallway, and sanctuary, and for the grace that met us in both laughter and loss over the years.

May the story God is writing in us continue to bring Him honor, and may the legacy of this church family keep shining from one generation to the next!

blocks.text:
Our family moved to Philadelphia from India in 1990. At that time, our family consisted of my wife, Rachel, our daughter Marina, and myself, Varughese. That same year, we joined SGMOC, which was worshipping at the Church of the Savior on 38th and Chestnut Streets. Mathai Achen and the church family welcomed us wholeheartedly and made us feel at home.

I have served as an Acolyte since 1968, having been ordained by the late Thoma Mar Dionysius of Niranam. After joining SGMOC, I continued this ministry and have been blessed with many opportunities to serve the Church, including multiple terms on the Board of Directors, Church Treasurer, Diocesan Assembly Member, and currently as a Malankara Association Member.

Our two younger daughters, Marilyn and Rosilyn, were both baptized at the Chestnut Street church and all three were actively involved in church life through the choir, Youth League, Sunday School, and other activities. My wife, Rachel, has also been a dedicated member of MMVS.

We are deeply grateful to God for the many blessings and opportunities He has given our family to worship, serve, and grow within this church community. As we celebrate 50 years of the Church's presence in Philadelphia, we give thanks for God's guidance and for the intercession of St. Mary, St. Thomas, and St. Gregorios. We pray for continued blessings upon our Church and its members for generations to come.

Our family has been part of the SGMOC family since 1993, and the church has always held a special place in our hearts. As a family, we witnessed the dedication and hard work of so many founding members, including my dad. Everyone gave their time, energy, and love to help build not just a church, but a true community and family.

As we celebrate 50 years, it is amazing to see how much SGMOC has grown under the guidance of our beloved spiritual fathers, Mathai Achen and Shibu Achen. We feel truly grateful and blessed to have been part of this journey. Wishing our entire SGMOC family a happy and blessed 50th anniversary. So grateful to celebrate this special milestone together, and praying for many more wonderful years ahead.

inMemoriam.name: V. Rev. Kaleeckal Mathai Cor Episcopos
inMemoriam.role: Founding Vicar • St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church
inMemoriam.text:
A visionary spiritual leader and devoted shepherd, Very Rev. Kaleeckal Mathai Cor Episcopos played a foundational role in establishing and nurturing the Malankara Orthodox community in Philadelphia. From his early calling to the priesthood, he dedicated his life to the Church, guiding the congregation through its formative years, growth, and the establishment of a permanent home in Bensalem. His unwavering faith, humility, compassion, and tireless dedication continue to inspire all of us.

Ordained as a deacon in **1974** and to the priesthood in **1975**, he served as the Founding Vicar of St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church from **1976** to **2011**. In **1996**, he was elevated to Cor Episcopos and also served the Northeast American Diocese as a Diocesan Council Member and Clergy Secretary.

members.name: Rev. Fr. Dr. Paul Varki
members.title: Rev. Fr. Dr. Paul Varki

inMemoriam.name: Rev. Fr. Dr. Paul Varki
inMemoriam.text:
Rev. Fr. Dr. Paul Varki was a pioneering spiritual leader whose dedication helped lay the foundation for Malankara Orthodox worship in the Philadelphia region. Beginning in 1965, he played an instrumental role in bringing Orthodox Christians together for worship, fostering an ecumenical fellowship that eventually contributed to the establishment of the parish in 1976.

After obtaining his Master of Divinity degree from Princeton Theological Seminary, he pursued further studies in psychology, earning his doctorate. His academic accomplishments complemented his spiritual calling, reflecting his lifelong commitment to faith, education, and service.

Through his vision, leadership, and tireless efforts, Fr. Paul Varki helped nurture the early Orthodox community in Philadelphia. His contributions remain an important part of the history of St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church and the spiritual heritage of generations who followed.

blocks.title: A Tribute to Rev. Fr. Dr. Paul Varki
blocks.text:
Rev. Fr. Dr. Paul Varki (formerly Dn. Paul Varki) faithfully served the Malankara Orthodox Church throughout his life. As we celebrate our Golden Jubilee, we lovingly remember a man whose devotion, humility, and steadfast service shaped the earliest foundations of our community.

Ordained as a deacon at age 18 by His Holiness Baselios Geevarghese II, he came to the United States in 1957 for higher studies. He pursued advanced academic work—including studies at Princeton University—and later earned a doctorate in Psychology. While serving as a Board-certified Psychologist for the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, he quietly nurtured the spiritual life of Malayalee Orthodox Christians in the region.

In 1965, he helped organize monthly worship at Asbury Church, hosting clergy from multiple denominations. This ecumenical fellowship became a spiritual home for Orthodox, Marthoma, Catholic, CSI, and other Kerala Christians for eleven years.

A turning point came in 1976, when he invited Rev. Fr. K. Mathai to lead Holy Week services. The overwhelming response led to the formation of the first Orthodox parish in Philadelphia. He later wrote to the Catholicos requesting authorization for a parish—resulting in the establishment of St. Thomas Orthodox Church of India (STOCI) on October 10, 1976.

The parish grew steadily, acquiring its first church building in Torresdale in 1984 and later building a new church in Bensalem, consecrated in 2009. As the new church neared completion, Paul Varki Achen reflected on the community’s journey with a joyful Malayalam poem:

അറുപത്തിനാലിൽ വിശ്വാസികൾ നട്ട മുന്തിരി വെസ്റ്റ് ഫിലിയിൽ
സെൻറ്‌ തോമസ് ആയി വന്നെല്ലോ
അതിനെ നനച്ചു വളർത്തി നാം സെൻറ്‌ ഗ്രീഗോറിയോസ് ആയി
ടോറസ്ഡെയിലിൽ ശോഭിച്ചു
[വീണ്ടും] ചേരുക നീ എൻ മാനസമേ
ബെൻസലേമിലെ നിലയത്തിൽ
പരുമല മരുവും തിരുമേനി വന്നു വസിക്കുന്നീ നാളിൽ
ഇന്നീ ജനന പെരുന്നാളിൽ
നാഥാ കരുണാ സാഗരമേ ഓർക്കണമേ നിൻ ജനതതിയെ

Rev. Fr. Dr. Paul Varki’s legacy is one of faithfulness, perseverance, and love. He helped build a community before there was a parish, welcomed clergy before there was a resident priest, and fostered unity long before there were church buildings. His memory remains a blessing to every Orthodox family in Greater Philadelphia.

blocks.text: My wife and I with our two children came to the United States of America on July 10, 1983.

My wife Mariam and I have been members of SGMOC since its very inception. We came to Delaware in 1975 for our respective Residency trainings. We joined the Malayalam services soon after we arrived — at first interdenominational — followed by a fellowship lunch at someone's home for which everyone contributed a dollar. The first Orthodox services started after the arrival of Rev. Fr. K. Mathai at the Chapel of what now is the Philadelphia Episcopal Cathedral at 38th and Chestnut Streets.

We were both born into Orthodox families, she in Secunderabad, I in Malaysia, and have attended Orthodox services all our lives. I attended the M. D. Seminary Higher Secondary School in Kottayam, then the location of the Orthodox Seminary. I was an Acolyte while at the Union Christian College, Alwaye. Rev. Fr. K. K. Mathews, who went on to be Barnabas Thirumeni, was our vicar while I studied at the Christian Medical College in Vellore.

We both are very proud of SGMOC for its dynamism, spirituality, community outreach and care for the members under the leadership of Rev. Fr. Shibu V. Mathai.

blocks.title: Memories of Our Early Years
blocks.text:
As America celebrates the 250th anniversary of its independence this year, we, as early Indian immigrants, are also celebrating our church’s Golden Jubilee, our 50th anniversary. We started our congregation in 1976 with the late Very Rev. Fr. K. Mathai Corepiscopa. Our first church was at 38th and Chestnut Streets in Philadelphia, the City of Brotherly Love. As we look back, we feel fortunate to have a new church in Bensalem Township.

We faced many hardships in the beginning. My wife joined the congregation in 1976, and I joined in 1977. Every Sunday, Mathai Achen celebrated the Holy Qurbana after blessing a small table as our Altar. Afterward, we had to pack everything up and take it home. This was very difficult because we had no permanent place to worship.

We remember cold Sunday mornings when we wanted to make coffee for the congregation. We all pitched in to buy the supplies and made the coffee in the small kitchen in the basement. The priest of the 38th Street Church, Fr. Hadvick, along with the custodian, helped us use the kitchen properly.

Our small group enjoyed organizing picnics and tours to Busch Gardens and Washington, D.C. Among the people I especially remember from those days are the late Mr. M.P. Paulose and Ms. Rachel Parel, who now resides in California.

Although we were not financially secure, we wanted a place of our own. We visited many properties, but we did not always have enough support. We tried to purchase a property on Verree Road in Northeast Philadelphia, but we could not obtain zoning approval, even though we had already laid a cornerstone. We then acquired a small property in Torresdale, where we held our services until we built our current church in Bensalem.

There are too many memories to mention here. As one of the early families, we worked hard for the church. I served as Treasurer and as a member of the Board of Trustees for many years, and my wife has been a dedicated member of the MMVS. I am happy to have seen this church grow over the years, and I hope it will continue to grow for the next generation.

Today, we are thankful to God Almighty for our larger and thriving church in Bensalem. This was possible only through the hard work of a core group of members in our church. We also cannot forget our former Bishops, H.G. Dr. Thomas Mar Makarios and H.G. Mathews Mar Barnabas, along with our founding priest, the late Very Rev. Fr. K. Mathai Corepiscopa.

May the prayers of all our Patron Saints and St. Mary, Mother of God, continue to bless us.

Finally, I am grateful to the Golden Jubilee Committee for allowing some of our old memories to be published.

blocks.text:
Jiji Koshy was born in the early 1960s and raised in Vazhoor, Kottayam, Kerala, as the youngest of eight children. His family was active in St. Peter’s Malankara Syrian Orthodox Church in Pulikkalkavala. After earning a degree in Business and Administration and working as a Logistics Manager in Kerala, Jiji immigrated to the United States in 1991, settling in New Jersey with his eldest brother, George.

Beena Abraham was born in the late 1960s and raised in North Paravur, Ernakulam, the second of three children of Areekal Abraham Tharian and Vazhappilli Sucy Abraham. After earning a master’s degree in physics, Beena married Jiji in 1992. Jiji settled in Philadelphia with his brother Thomas, where he helped establish St. Mary’s Malankara Syrian Orthodox Church; Beena and their daughter Jane joined him in 1996.

In the summer of 2000, a season of change — a new job, a new home, their eldest starting kindergarten and a third child on the way — brought them to St. Gregorios, shortly before Joanne was born. Over the years both became active in the ministries, and their daughters in the Youth League and Sunday School. In 2023 Beena made parish history as the first woman to serve as Treasurer and Trustee.

Jiji grew up serving at the altar in his home parish, and after immigrating faced pressure from colleagues and family to join other denominations. He stayed with the faith handed down to him, and encourages those around him to do the same. Beena set out to be a physicist and found instead a profession in computers; leaving her family in Kerala, she built a new one here, and came to find in SGMOC a second home.

Jiji established and runs Alma Digital Vision, his photography and videography business, and Beena works as an Enterprise Systems Programmer with the City of Philadelphia. Their daughters have gone on to science research, engineering, literature and writing. Above all the family treasures the church community that has carried and enriched their lives.

blocks.text:
Paul C Mathai, founding member of St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church in Philadelphia, has been a member of the church since its inception, serving in numerous leadership roles including Treasurer, Secretary, Board of Trustee and Committee Member.

He, along with his wife Joan and their children Stephen and Kristine, has been an active supporter of the church’s mission and congregation. By the grace of God and the support of friends and family, the Paul C. Mathai Scholarship Fund was established fifteen years ago, to encourage the youth of our church to pursue higher education and to serve the greater Orthodox community.

The Paul C. Mathai family extends our congratulations to our church on this 50th Jubilee Anniversary year. May God continue to bless our church and all its members forever.

blocks.text:
As a couple in our 50s who have raised our children and recently been blessed through Holy Matrimony, joining St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church two years ago has marked a beautiful new chapter in our spiritual journey.

As we look at our family gathered together for our wedding in this photograph, taken within the walls of this church, we are filled with gratitude for the warm embrace and loving fellowship of this parish. It is truly a privilege to celebrate our family's joy alongside the historic Golden Jubilee of our church.

Thank you for welcoming us into fifty years of sacred heritage, steadfast faith, and apostolic witness. We look forward to many more years of fellowship as we continue to walk together in Christ.
The Lord has done great things for us, and we are filled with joy.

We pray that Almighty God continues to bless St. Gregorios Church, preserving its rich apostolic heritage and guiding generations to come.

May the light of this altar continue to shine brightly, welcoming all into Christ's love for the next fifty years and beyond.

blocks.title: Message from the family of Dr. T. V. and Mary Philip
blocks.text: The very first regular worship services in the Philadelphia area for the Malankara Orthodox Church (which at that time was still named the Syrian Orthodox Church of India) were held in an apartment at 49th & Pine in the early 1960s. This was the apartment where Dr TV Philip lived with his wife, Mary (Marykutty), and infant son, George, and eventually his younger brother, John. The priest, who Dr Philip invited regularly to Philadelphia from New York City, was Rev Fr. KM Simon (later, the Very Reverend Fr. KM Simon, Cor Episcopa.  By the way, Simon Achan baptized Georgie as the very first out of the hundreds of baptisms he eventually performed in the US, before his passing in 1996). These initial worship services were ecumenical; there were just a handful of Malayalis in the entire Philadelphia area at that time, and all of them attended the services. These services were also the beginning of a long line of different locations and congregations that eventually led to the founding of the St Thomas Orthodox Church in 1976 with Rev Fr. K Mathai Achan as its vicar, (later, Very Rev. K. Mathai Cor Episcopa).  Later, the parish became the St Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church in Bensalem. In 1966, the family moved to Reading PA, where Neena (now married to Chris) was born. After the move to Reading, they had to drive about 1.5 hours each way to attend regular worship services in Philadelphia. Despite the distances, and the challenges with Johnny’s severe autism, they remained fully active in many church activities, including regular attendance at the Diocese Family Conference. Dr Philip was pleased to serve for 5 years as the official Auditor of the North American Diocese under His Grace Barnabas-Thirumeni in the early 2000s. As a very happy grandfather of Nathaniel and Isaac, Dr Philip lived 90 healthy and active years, passing away in June 2014, just weeks after celebrating his 90th birthday at the church. Marykutty was well loved by church members and passed away in June 2022 at age 88.  On September 13th 2026, Shibu Achan was kind enough to celebrate Johnny’s 63rd birthday and his Pioneer status at St Gregorios.

blocks.title: Our Family's Journey at SGMOC
blocks.text:
Our journey with SGMOC began in 2023 with the appointment of Ceena Mathew as the Associate Minister of the parish. Shibu Achen and the church family warmly welcomed Dr. Mathew, Ceena, and Joseph in March 2023. Ceena’s parents, Rev. Fr. K. P. Varghese and Rosamma Varghese, joined SGMOC after moving from Baltimore to Pennsylvania in 2024. After Benjamin was born, he was blessed to be baptized at this church in May 2025. Mathew’s parents, Dr. M. I. John and Prof. Rajamma John, worshipped at SGMOC for a few months during their visit in 2025. Another special blessing was celebrating the 50th anniversary of Varghese Achen’s priesthood at SGMOC in November 2025.

We are thankful to the parish community for welcoming us and we are especially grateful to Shibu Achen for inviting us to serve alongside him in the ministries of the church and for giving us the opportunity to be part of this wonderful parish family. As we continue this journey together, we look forward to growing in Christ through the sacramental life of the Church, through service, and through the fellowship and love we share with one another. May the intercession of St. Gregorios of Parumala and the abundant grace of our Lord Jesus Christ continue to guide and bless SGMOC for generations to come.
May the intercessions of the Holy Theotokos, St. Joseph, Patriarch Joseph and Patriarch Benjamin be a refuge for us!
